newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip rally stalls, but small-name companies soar.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip rally stalls, but small-name companies soar.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks barely held their ground Monday, under pressure from profit-taking after last week's spectacular rally, while small-name companies jumped.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 6.82 points, or 0.10 percent, at 7,078.02, pausing after soaring 332 points last week in their biggest weekly gain ever.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 2-1 on volume of 290 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 11/32, which raised its yield to 6.91 percent from 6.88 percent on Friday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

The Nasdaq Composite Index, which is dominated by small-name companies, was up 20.09, or 1.50 percent, at 1,325.42. The Russell 2000 index, another gauge of smaller capitalisation issues, was up 6.67 points, or 1.88 percent, at 360.65.
"There is no question that the small caps are having one heck of a day," said Anthony O'Bryan, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
The move in small capitalisation stocks, which have languished since the start of the year, is a welcome one, broadening the base of a previously narrow rally, analysts said.
Through last Friday, the Dow industrials had risen 9.7 percent so far this year, but the Nasdaq Composite index has inched up only 1.1 percent and the Russell 2000 has fallen 2.4 percent.
The numbers include impressive gains by the two smaller-cap indexes on Friday.
"When the Dow becomes expensive, which it has, you start to see a move in secondary stocks," said Hugh Johsnon, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"Small caps are catching up because the large cap lift has been picked over, and there is not much to be found by way of values. The techs are a meaningful part of the small cap universe."
High technology stocks put in a strong showing.

Cisco Systems Inc., the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 1-5/8 at 58-7/8, Oracle Corp. rose 1-7/8 to 44-3/8, Intel Corp. gained 3-3/8 to 161, Netscape Communications Corp. rose 3 to 31-1/8 and International Business Machines Corp. added 1-3/4 to 164.

"A lot of this is due to momentum. As soon as you begin to see some momentum in the techs or in the small caps, momentum investors start entering the picture," Johnson said. "The techs aren't being driven by any meaningful change in the fundamental outlook which is positive."
Ascend Communications Inc. rose 2-3/4 to 52-5/8 after Soundview Financial Group said it raised its rating on the shares.
